confirmed.title: PARALLEL_SIMS=2 is fatal: relay serves one TCP client at a time, second collector dies after 300s with zero episodes
confirmed.claim: collect() launches two 16_collect_distill.py processes against relay port 8767, but 15_winner_relay.py accepts one connection and serves it to completion before calling accept() again; the second sim's first recv blocks past its 300s socket timeout, raises, and exits having collected nothing. Roughly every other (garment, chunk) job is silently wasted and its garment never reaches target.
confirmed.evidence: orchestrator.py:63 PARALLEL_SIMS=2; :263-266 launches up to PARALLEL_SIMS Popen at once. 15_winner_relay.py:178 `srv.listen(1)`; :183-211 `while True: conn,addr = await ...srv.accept()` then inner `while True: msg = ...recv_msg(conn)` — accept() is only reached again after the inner loop ends (disconnect). Single shared `policy = WinnerPolicy(ws)` (:173) and session_id 'isaac' (:104) also mean two clients could not be multiplexed even if accepted. 16_collect_distill.py:129 `conn.settimeout(300.0)`, :186-187 send reset then recv_msg -> socket.timeout -> :312 `except Exception` -> app.close(). Orchestrator reap() (:245-257) logs 'done' and launches the next job into the same dead slot.
confirmed.fix: Set PARALLEL_SIMS default to 1 until the relay is made per-connection (one WinnerPolicy + unique session_id per accepted socket, run each connection in its own task/thread). Alternatively start one relay per sim on distinct ports and pass --port per job.
votes:
CONFIRMED by reading the exact code path; the failure scenario occurs as described (and is actually worse than "every other job").

Relay side (C:\Users\H\Desktop\lehome-win\15_winner_relay.py): one listening socket with `srv.listen(1)` (l.178). The outer `while True` awaits `srv.accept` (l.184) and then enters an inner `while True` (l.188-206) that awaits `recv_msg`/`policy.act` INLINE (`await loop.run_in_executor(...)`, no task spawning), so accept() is only reached again after the inner loop exits via recv None / ConnectionReset -> `finally: conn.close()` (l.209-211). A single shared `policy = WinnerPolicy(ws)` (l.173) with one queue/garment_id/step and a hard-coded session_id "isaac" (l.104) means two clients could not be interleaved even if accepted. There is no per-connection concurrency anywhere.

Client side (16_collect_distill.py): scene is built first (l.116-118), then `conn.connect` (l.126) — a queued connection completes its handshake in-kernel (or, if the Windows backlog is full, is refused with ConnectionRefusedError; either way fatal). `conn.settimeout(300.0)` (l.129). First episode: `send_msg(reset)` (l.186) then `recv_msg(conn)` (l.187) -> `c.recv` (l.76) blocks; recv_msg has no try/except, so socket.timeout propagates to the module-level `except Exception` (l.312-320), which logs the traceback and deletes the orphan ep_dir, then `app.close()` (l.322). No retry/reconnect logic exists (grep confirms). Result: process exits with n_kept=0, zero meta.json written.

Orchestrator side (orchestrator.py): `PARALLEL_SIMS` default 2 (l.63); the dispatch loop (l.259-280) launches jobs whenever `len(running) < PARALLEL_SIMS`, all with `--port 8767` (l.277). `reap()` (l.245-257) treats any `poll() is not None` as "done" regardless of exit status/episodes, frees the slot, and the next job is launched into it.

Timing makes it certain: collect_auto.log shows 50-104 s per episode and a job allows up to 63 attempts (e.g. 21-keep target), so a served job holds the relay for >1 h, while a starved job dies after ~1.5 min scene load + 300 s. Hence, during one served job, the other slot burns ~10+ queued jobs in succession, not just one — in a typical collect() call (2 chunks x ~9 garments = 18 jobs) most of the queue is consumed by the starved slot and only 1-2 jobs actually collect data. Secondary hazard: `ensure_teacher()`'s `port_open(8767)` probe (l.92) itself occupies the backlog-1 queue; if refused, the orchestrator spawns a second relay bound to 8767 (SO_REUSEADDR on Windows permits this).

No empirical refutation: orchestrator.log shows only one collect job ever launched (08-26, pre-parallel format); run_collect3.ps1 and the running weekend.ps1 stage C both run clients strictly sequentially (WaitForExit per chunk/garment), so the two-client case has never been exercised. affects_running_chain=false is correct (weekend.ps1/curation.ps1 do not use orchestrator.py and never open two 8767 clients at once). Proposed fix (PARALLEL_SIMS default 1, or per-connection policy/session or one relay per port) is appropriate.

Confirmed from code. orchestrator.py:63 defaults PARALLEL_SIMS=2 and :263-280 launches up to two 16_collect_distill.py processes all hardcoded to --port 8767 (:277). 15_winner_relay.py:178 listen(1); :183-211 accept() -> inner recv loop that only returns to accept() on disconnect; single WinnerPolicy (:173) and single session_id 'isaac' (:104), so it cannot serve two clients. 16_collect_distill.py:129 settimeout(300) then :186-187 send reset + recv_msg on the un-accepted socket -> socket.timeout -> :312 except Exception -> app.close() with exit code 0; orchestrator reap() (:245-257) only checks poll(), logs 'done' and refills the slot. Because job 1 holds the relay for up to 3h, every job cycled through slot 2 dies in ~5 min + Isaac boot, so the loss is actually worse than 'every other job'. Impact is latent, however: all past collections (run_collect*.ps1) and the running weekend.ps1 Stage C use Start-Process + WaitForExit (serial, one relay client), so no measured number or the current chain is affected; orchestrator.log shows the only prior run (08-26) launched one job and stopped before slot 2 filled (state.json still cycle 0/collect). It would waste GPU-hours (starved collect stage followed by ~8h training on under-filled data) only when orchestrator.py is next run with the default. One-line fix: default --parallel-sims to 1 (or per-connection relay / one relay port per sim).

Confirmed from code. 15_winner_relay.py:178 listen(1); :183-211 accept() then an inner `while True` that only exits on client disconnect/quit, so accept() is never re-entered while a client is served; one shared WinnerPolicy (:173) with a single queue/step/garment_id and fixed session_id 'isaac' (:104) rules out multiplexing. orchestrator.py:63 PARALLEL_SIMS=2 and :259-280 launch two 16_collect_distill.py processes both on --port 8767; reap() (:245-257) only checks poll() and logs 'done', never return code or episode count. 16_collect_distill.py:129 settimeout(300), :186-187 sends reset then blocks in recv; socket.timeout (or ConnectionRefusedError if the 1-deep backlog is stale-filled) hits :312 `except Exception` -> app.close() -> exit 0 with zero episodes. Alternatives rejected: (a) first job cannot finish within 300 s (>=20 target successes, up to 3x attempts, up to 600 teacher steps with 3 JPEG saves each); (b) backlog refusal vs. timeout both land in the same except path; (c) ensure_teacher() only ever starts one relay on 8767. No empirical counter-evidence: orchestrator.log shows a single older serial-format run that launched one job and died; the parallel path has never executed. Impact is worse than 'every other job': slot 2 cycles through jobs every ~5-8 min while slot 1 runs for hours, so most of the 18-job list can be consumed with nothing collected. weekend.ps1 stage C runs 22_replay_snapshots.py serially (WaitForExit) and curation.ps1 does not use 8767, so the running chain is unaffected.

confirmed.title: train() 8h watchdog is shorter than any measured 60k-step run; batch 48 cannot finish
confirmed.claim: Measured checkpoint timestamps show ~3h per 20k steps at batch 16 (9h for 60k) and ~1h22 per 15k at batch 16 on an idle GPU (5.5h/60k). The orchestrator uses batch 48 (3x the samples per step) with an 8h timeout, so the run is taskkilled before checkpoints/060000 exists, train() returns None and main() exits ('학습 실패 — 종료') after burning 8 GPU-hours.
confirmed.evidence: orchestrator.py:57 TRAIN_BATCH=48, :56 TRAIN_STEPS=60000, :387 `run(cmd, timeout=8 * 3600, ...)`, :389-391 requires checkpoints/060000/pretrained_model. outputs/act_student_r3plus_aug/checkpoints mtimes: 020000 08-26 19:38, 040000 22:40, 060000 01:43 (3h02 per 20k, batch 16). outputs/act_student_big45/checkpoints: 015000 22:03, 030000 23:25, 045000 00:48 (1h22 per 15k, batch 16). run() on timeout: :110-114 taskkill /T /F and returns (-1, True).
confirmed.fix: Either raise the train timeout to >= 30h (or remove it and rely on checkpoint-existence), or drop TRAIN_BATCH to 16 and set timeout >= 12h. Also consider returning the latest existing checkpoint instead of None on timeout.
votes: CONFIRMED by reading the exact code path and measured timing. Code: orchestrator.py:56-57 TRAIN_STEPS=60000 / TRAIN_BATCH=48; :365 passes --batch_size=48 with --num_workers=4; :379-380 turns image_transforms ON; :382-383 adds --dataset.eval_split=0.05 --eval_steps=200 --max_eval_samples=2000 (these args ARE valid in this patched lerobot: configs/train.py:109-111, configs/default.py:48, so training does not fail fast); :387 run(cmd, timeout=8*3600); run() :108-114 taskkills the tree on TimeoutExpired and returns (-1, True); :389-391 returns None unless checkpoints/060000/pretrained_model exists; main() :612-614 logs '학습 실패 — 종료' and returns on None. Checkpoint mtimes match the finding exactly (r3plus_aug 20k/40k/60k at 19:38/22:40/01:43 = 3h02 per 20k; big45 1h22 per 15k). Per-step timing from the lerobot logs pins the cause: lerobot_train.py:567-568 measures data_s as the wait on next(dl_iter). aug_train_err.log (verified in its config dump: batch_size 16, image_transforms enable True, max_num_transforms 3, use_amp False - the same loader setup the orchestrator uses) shows mean updt_s=0.160 + data_s=0.424 = 0.58 s/step (9.7h/60k, matching the mtimes). A non-zero data_s means the 4-worker augmented loader is saturated at ~28 samples/s; at batch 48 that is ~1.7 s/step => ~29h for 60k steps. Even using the fastest measured loader (no-aug train_student_err.log, ~68 samples/s) gives 0.71 s/step => ~11.8h, still over 8h, and the 300 held-out eval passes (60000/200 x up to 2000 samples) add more loader work. AMP only shortens updt_s, not data_s. So under every measured rate the 060000 checkpoint cannot exist at 8h; train() returns None and the loop exits after ~8 GPU-hours. It compounds on rerun: state stays at stage 'train', outputs/act_student_<tag> now exists, and lerobot configs/train.py:236-239 raises FileExistsError without --resume, so every retry fails instantly. state.json (cycle 0, stage collect) and orchestrator.log (no train lines) confirm this path has never executed, so it is latent and does not touch the running weekend.ps1 chain (batch 16).

Confirmed from code and logs. orchestrator.py:56-57 sets TRAIN_STEPS=60000 / TRAIN_BATCH=48, :365 pins --num_workers=4, :387 runs lerobot-train with timeout=8*3600, :389-391 only accepts checkpoints/060000/pretrained_model, run() :110-114 taskkills the tree on timeout, and main() :612-614 exits on None. Measured throughput is a data-loader ceiling, not a GPU limit: train_all700b_resume.log (batch 16, workers 4, fp32, dim512) shows updt_s 0.163 + data_s 0.165 = 0.33 s/step = 49 smp/s; train_big45.log (dim640/8 layers, ~2x FLOPs, same workers) shows updt_s 0.232 + data_s 0.099 = 0.33 s/step = 49 smp/s -- identical wall time despite double compute, so the 4-worker image-transform pipeline pins the step. The AMP run (train_all700.err.log, use_amp=True) is even slower at 31-40 smp/s, so --policy.use_amp=true does not lift it. Checkpoint mtimes agree (all700b 40k->60k in 1h49, big45 1h22/15k, both 3.05 steps/s). No batch-48 run has ever been executed (outputs/ has only batch-16 runs; AUDIT.md row 5 lists batch 48 as planned), so the 3x figure is extrapolation, but the data-bound floor alone gives 60000*48/49 = 2.88M samples / 49 = ~16.3h, plus --eval_steps=200 with max_eval_samples=2000 pushes ~600k extra samples through the loader (lerobot_train.py:618-634) -> ~18-20h. At the 8h kill only checkpoints/020000 (~5.4h) exists, train() returns None, main exits. Compounding: state.json stays at stage 'train' and outputs/act_student_auto1 already exists, so a re-run hits lerobot configs/train.py:236-240 FileExistsError (resume=False) and fails instantly -- the loop cannot self-recover without manual cleanup. Impact scope: no reported number depends on this (orchestrator never ran end-to-end), and the running weekend chain is unaffected (no .ps1 references orchestrator.py; train_cur.log is a separate batch-16 run). It is a deterministic >=8 GPU-hour waste plus a dead-end on the first orchestrator cycle, fixed by one constant -- serious, but not critical for currently measured results or the live chain.

Confirmed from code and logs. orchestrator.py:56-57 sets TRAIN_STEPS=60000/TRAIN_BATCH=48, :387 wraps lerobot-train in run(timeout=8*3600) which taskkills the tree on expiry (:110-114), :389-391 returns None unless checkpoints/060000/pretrained_model exists, and main() :612-614 aborts on None ('학습 실패 — 종료'). Checkpoint mtimes match the finding (r3plus_aug 3h02/20k; big45 1h22/15k; all700b resume 1h49/20k = best case 0.33 s/step at batch 16 -> 5.5 h/60k). Alternative explanations fail: lerobot_train.py:567-584 runs dataloading then update sequentially, and every measured run logs data_s >= updt_s (r3plus_aug 0.391 vs 0.153; current curation run ~0.22 vs 0.150), i.e. the 4 CPU dataloader workers (video decode + image transforms, aug ON) are the bottleneck at ~43-49 samples/s. AMP (use_amp=true) only shrinks updt_s and cannot raise worker throughput; a bigger batch does not reduce per-sample cost. Batch 48 x 60k = 2.88M samples / ~49 samples/s = ~16 h minimum, and the orchestrator also adds --eval_steps=200 --max_eval_samples=2000 through a second dataloader with the same num_workers/batch_size (lerobot_train.py:492-502), ~600k more samples (~3 h). Fitting 8 h would need ~100 samples/s, double anything measured. The eval flags exist in this editable lerobot 0.6.1 (configs/train.py:109-111, default.py:48), so it will not fail fast on a parse error; it will run until killed. Caveat: state.json (cycle 0, stage collect) and orchestrator.log (single start line) show the train stage has never executed, so this is a projection from batch-16 measurements, not an observed timeout. It does not affect the running weekend/curation chain, which uses batch_size=16 via its own scripts.

confirmed.title: Resume in stage 'train' always fails: output_dir already exists -> lerobot FileExistsError
confirmed.claim: If the process dies or times out during training and state.json says stage='train', re-running the orchestrator re-invokes lerobot-train with the same --output_dir. lerobot 0.6.1 raises FileExistsError when output_dir exists and resume=false, so every rerun fails identically and the loop is permanently stuck (this compounds the 8h-timeout defect).
confirmed.evidence: orchestrator.py:356 `out = os.path.join(HERE, 'outputs', f'act_student_{tag}')`, :360 `--output_dir={out}`; no --resume/--config_path and no rmtree of `out`. lerobot/src/lerobot/configs/train.py:236-240 `if not self.resume and ... self.output_dir.is_dir(): raise FileExistsError(...)`. main() :606-614 re-enters train() on stage=='train' and exits on None.
confirmed.fix: In train(): if `out` exists, either delete it (fresh restart) or resume via `--resume=true --config_path=<out>/checkpoints/last/pretrained_model/train_config.json`; record which was done in state.json.
votes:
CONFIRMED by reading the exact code path, with one scope qualification.

Code path (orchestrator.py, C:\Users\H\Desktop\lehome-win\orchestrator.py):
- :568-570 tag = f"auto{st['cycle']+1}"; st['cycle'] is only advanced at :645 after a successful eval, so a rerun in stage 'train' reuses the same tag.
- :356 out = HERE/outputs/act_student_{tag}; :361 "--output_dir={out}". The cmd never includes --resume or --config_path; the only rmtree in the file (:322) is for the merged dataset dir, never for `out`.
- :387-391 run() ignores the return code; train() returns None unless out/checkpoints/060000/pretrained_model exists.
- :606-614 main() re-enters train() whenever stage=='train' and returns (process exit) on None, leaving state.json at stage='train'.

lerobot side (C:\Users\H\Desktop\lerobot\src\lerobot\configs\train.py:236-240): `if not self.resume and isinstance(self.output_dir, Path) and self.output_dir.is_dir(): raise FileExistsError(...)` — raised in validate() at config-parse time, before any training. resume defaults to False (:92).

When does `out` exist? lerobot_train.py writes to cfg.output_dir only via save_checkpoint at is_saving_step = step % save_freq == 0 or step == cfg.steps (:593, :641-653; train_utils.save_checkpoint mkdirs). init_logging is called without log_file (:224) and wandb is disabled, so nothing else creates the dir. With --save_freq=20000 and TRAIN_STEPS=60000, `out` exists iff training reached step 20000 (or 40000).

So the failure scenario is real: die/timeout after step >=20000 -> `out` exists -> every rerun hits FileExistsError inside lerobot-train -> no 060000 checkpoint -> train() returns None -> main exits -> state stays 'train' -> permanently stuck until someone manually deletes/renames outputs/act_student_autoN. This defeats the file's own stated design goal (docstring :4 — resume from any point).

Qualification: the word "always" overstates it. A crash before step 20000 leaves no output_dir, so the rerun starts fresh (wastes the partial run, but does not wedge). For the 8h-timeout case on a 60k-step run, having passed 20k is the overwhelmingly likely situation, so the practical impact matches the claim.

Not yet triggered on disk: state.json is at cycle 0 / stage 'collect' and no outputs/act_student_auto* dir exists; the running weekend.ps1 chain does not go through orchestrator.py, so affects_running_chain=false is correct.

Fix note: the proposed --resume=true --config_path=<out>/checkpoints/last/pretrained_model/train_config.json is viable — this lerobot tree honors an explicit --output_dir on resume (train.py:200-202) and update_last_checkpoint (train_utils.py:85-116) falls back to a junction on Windows, but if both symlink and junction fail it writes last.txt instead of a `last` dir, so the resumer should fall back to the highest-numbered checkpoints/<step> dir rather than rely solely on `last`.

Confirmed from code. orchestrator.py train() (lines 356-361) always passes a fixed --output_dir=outputs/act_student_{tag} with no --resume/--config_path and no rmtree; on timeout/death run() returns -1, ck (checkpoints/060000) is missing, train() returns None, main() exits at 613-614 with state.json still at stage='train'. Re-running re-enters train() with the same tag; lerobot 0.6.1 (venv is an editable install of C:\Users\H\Desktop\lerobot\src) raises FileExistsError in TrainPipelineConfig.validate() (configs/train.py:236-240) whenever output_dir exists and resume is false, before any training. output_dir is only created by the checkpoint save (lerobot_train.py:652, save_freq=20000), so the trap arms once a run passes 20k steps and then dies. The trigger is realistic: all logged runs are batch 16 at ~180 steps/min regardless of model size (dataloader-bound), so the orchestrator's batch-48/60k-step run (~16h) will exceed the 8h timeout at ~29k steps, past the 20k checkpoint. Every subsequent rerun then fails identically; the orchestrator's documented resume-anywhere guarantee is broken at the train stage. Rollback path (--policy.pretrained_path) does not change output_dir either. Severity lowered rather than kept: no measured number is affected, the rerun is fail-fast (no GPU burned), the running weekend/curation chain never invokes orchestrator.py, state.json is still at cycle 0/stage collect (no act_student_auto* dir exists, bug latent), and manual recovery is a one-liner (delete dir or --resume=true --config_path=.../checkpoints/last/pretrained_model/train_config.json, as recover700b.ps1 already does). Real cost is lost unattended wall-clock and manual intervention, which is medium, not high.

Confirmed in code. orchestrator.py:356-361 passes a fixed --output_dir=outputs/act_student_{tag} with no --resume/--config_path, no existence check and no rmtree (the only rmtree at :322 is the merged dataset dir; the resume_from arg at :384 is a --policy.pretrained_path rollback, not a lerobot resume). The venv is an editable install of C:\Users\H\Desktop\lerobot\src (__editable__.lerobot-0.6.1.pth), whose configs/train.py:236-240 raises FileExistsError in validate() when output_dir exists and resume is False; validate() runs at lerobot_train.py:203 before any training. main() :606-614 returns on ck=None without changing stage, so every rerun repeats the same failing command. One narrowing nuance: output_dir is only created by save_checkpoint (train_utils.py:171-173,218), gated by step % save_freq == 0 or step == steps (lerobot_train.py:593); init_logging has no log file, eval_split writes nothing, and env video output is disabled. With save_freq=20000 a crash before step 20000 leaves no dir and the rerun restarts from scratch (wasteful, not stuck). The permanent stall therefore applies whenever the failed attempt reached >=20000 steps, which is exactly the 8h-timeout case and the observed 'killed at 61%' incident pattern. So 'always fails' is overstated, but the core defect stands. No current impact: state.json is at cycle 0/stage collect and no outputs/act_student_auto* dir exists.

confirmed.title: --policy.optimizer_lr_backbone=1e-5 is dead with use_policy_training_preset=false; backbone trains at 1e-4 peak
confirmed.claim: When use_policy_training_preset=false, lerobot builds the optimizer from policy.parameters() (single param group), not policy.get_optim_params(); the ACT per-group backbone LR is never applied. The pretrained ResNet18 backbone therefore gets the full 1e-4 cosine peak — the same LR regime the project already recorded as collapsing training (all700 lr 1e-4 -> 3.3%).
confirmed.evidence: orchestrator.py:370-374 passes `--use_policy_training_preset=false`, `--policy.optimizer_lr=1e-4`, `--policy.optimizer_lr_backbone=1e-5`, scheduler peak_lr=1e-4 (:378). lerobot/src/lerobot/optim/factory.py:37 `params = policy.get_optim_params() if cfg.use_policy_training_preset else policy.parameters()`. modeling_act.py:72-86 get_optim_params is the only place backbone lr is split out. 26_check_train_args.py never prints optimizer param groups, so this was not caught.
confirmed.fix: Either keep preset=false and add an explicit param-group mechanism (not available via CLI in 0.6.1 — would need a small wrapper script), or lower --optimizer.lr / --scheduler.peak_lr to the proven 1e-5 recipe and accept a uniform LR. At minimum remove the misleading --policy.optimizer_lr* flags.
votes: CONFIRMED by reading the exact path and by a CPU-only reproduction (no GPU, no edits). (1) The venv's lerobot is the editable checkout C:\Users\H\Desktop\lerobot\src (0.6.1); optim/factory.py:37 is verbatim `params = policy.get_optim_params() if cfg.use_policy_training_preset else policy.parameters()`, and configs/train.py:249-253 only substitutes the policy presets when the flag is True, so with `--use_policy_training_preset=false` (orchestrator.py:370) the optimizer is built from `policy.parameters()`. (2) optim/optimizers.py:108-111 `AdamWConfig.build` passes that iterable straight to `torch.optim.AdamW(params, lr=1e-4, ...)` -> one param group. (3) policies/act/modeling_act.py:72-91 `get_optim_params` is the only consumer of `config.optimizer_lr_backbone`; `config.optimizer_lr` is only read by `get_optimizer_preset` (configuration_act.py:153-157), which is also skipped. So orchestrator.py:373-374 are dead flags. (4) schedulers.py:163-182 is a multiplicative LambdaLR on each group's base lr, so the single group ramps to peak 1e-4. Reproduction (ACTPolicy + TrainPipelineConfig, orchestrator's exact optimizer/scheduler values): preset=False -> groups=1, 51,597,190 params incl. `model.backbone.conv1.weight` (11.17M trainable backbone params; only BatchNorm is frozen), lr 9.98e-05 at step 2000, 5.5e-05 at 30k, 1e-05 at 60k; preset=True -> 2 groups with backbone at 1e-5. Minor caveats: the finding's causal link (backbone LR alone caused the 3.3%) is not proven — all700 also differed in AMP/scheduler/batch, and batch 48 may be more tolerant than 16 — but the code claim (flag dead, backbone at 1e-4 peak) is fully correct. affects_running_chain=false is also correct: weekend.ps1/curation.ps1 pass no optimizer/preset flags (preset=True, 1e-5) and do not call orchestrator.py.

confirmed.title: Server binds with SO_REUSEADDR on Windows and Full-Eval never verifies the port is free/up -> a surviving old server can silently serve the wrong checkpoint
confirmed.claim: On Windows, SO_REUSEADDR (unlike Linux) lets a second socket bind and listen on 127.0.0.1:8766 while another process is still listening there; which listener receives a given connect is then indeterminate. Stop-Student kills by a CIM CommandLine regex and never checks that 8766 is actually closed, and Full-Eval in weekend.ps1 (unlike the sweeps) has no PortUp check at all — it sleeps 45 s and launches run_full_bench.ps1. If the kill misses (CommandLine unreadable, process in the middle of exiting, or a server started by another tool), the new server starts without error and benchmarks may be answered by the stale model with no log trace — the same class of incident already seen once ('evaluated wrong model'). Secondary: if checkpoint load takes >45 s, all 12 first-pass garments fail to connect (12 Isaac boots wasted) before the retry loop rescues them.
confirmed.evidence: 12_policy_server.py:125-128 `srv.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1); srv.bind((HOST, PORT)); srv.listen(1)`. weekend.ps1:13-17 Stop-Student (regex kill + 5 s sleep, no port check), :32-38 Full-Eval: Stop-Student, Start-Process server, `Start-Sleep -Seconds 45`, then run_full_bench.ps1 with no PortUp call (compare run_infer_sweep.ps1:49-52 which does check). curation.ps1:31-42 identical pattern. Windows semantics: Microsoft 'Using SO_REUSEADDR and SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE' — SO_REUSEADDR allows binding to a port already in use unless the first socket used SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE.
confirmed.fix: In 12_policy_server.py use `SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE` (socket.SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE) instead of SO_REUSEADDR so a duplicate bind fails loudly; have the server print the checkpoint path on every connection and have 14_benchmark log the `image_keys`/ckpt returned in the reset reply. confirmed.title: Fixed 60k-step budget confounds every data-scaling comparison: 700-ep models are undertrained (8 epochs) vs the 267-ep champion (21 epochs)
confirmed.claim: All recipes use --steps=60000 --batch_size=16 regardless of dataset size, so samples/frame differ 2.6x: r3plus (44,700 frames) gets 21.5 epochs, all700 (116,010) 8.3, big45 6.2, the running cur (84,405) 11.4. Training loss confirms the 700-ep models never reached the champion's fit: r3plus_aug ended at 0.126, all700b/c at 0.172 (a level r3plus_aug passed at ~30K steps), big45 at 0.174. 'More data scored lower' is therefore a comparison of an undertrained model against a converged one, not evidence against data scaling. curation.ps1 and weekend stages B/D/E inherit the same fixed budget.

confirmed.title: chunk_size=100 with n_action_steps=5: 30% of supervised targets are padding, 95% of the predicted horizon is discarded; chunk 30 is a sound but not-yet-run experiment with a CLI trap
confirmed.claim: Episodes are median 135 frames at 30 fps, so a 100-step chunk overruns the episode end for 64.6% of frames and 29.9% of all action targets are `action_is_pad` (masked, zero gradient); the L1 loss weights the remaining 1-100 step horizon uniformly while inference executes only steps 1-5. Training with chunk_size 30 (the winner's 30-step/1 s chunk) cuts padding to 8.7% and focuses capacity on the executed horizon. It requires a fresh run (decoder position embedding is sized by chunk_size) and BOTH `--policy.chunk_size=30 --policy.n_action_steps=30` — passing chunk_size alone raises ValueError because the default n_action_steps=100 exceeds it. No chain currently sets chunk_size.

confirmed.title: Ensure-Teacher treats a stale relay as healthy after a teacher restart -> first stage-C garment after a teacher death is lost
confirmed.claim: Ensure-Teacher only checks TCP listeners. If the WSL teacher (8000) dies and is restarted by the wsl command, the already-running relay (PIDs 36832/32860, up since 09-04) still listens on 8767 while its websocket to the old server is dead, so `PortUp 8767` passes and the function returns true. 22_replay then connects; the relay's first `policy.act` raises websockets ConnectionClosed, which is not in the relay's `except (ConnectionResetError, ConnectionAbortedError)`, so the relay process exits; 22_replay's recv_msg returns None and `rsp["action"]` raises TypeError -> EXCEPTION -> that garment's recovery run is lost. The next loop iteration restarts the relay, so the damage is one garment (~up to 50 min) per teacher death. The wsl command itself is correct: paths /root/.local/bin/uv, scripts/serve.py and checkpoints/lehome_sim exist, WSL default user is root, and the arguments match the currently running serve.py exactly.
confirmed.evidence: weekend.ps1:19-29 (checks `PortUp 8000` then `PortUp 8767` independently, returns `(PortUp 8000) -and (PortUp 8767)`). 15_winner_relay.py:169 `async with websockets.connect(WS_URL, ...) as ws:` wraps the whole TCP accept loop; :207 `except (ConnectionResetError, ConnectionAbortedError): pass` only. 22_replay_snapshots.py:231-232 `rsp = recv_msg(conn); act = np.asarray(rsp["action"], ...)` with no None check. WSL check (read-only): `whoami` = root; serve.py running as `uv run python scripts/serve.py --port 8000 --num_rollout_candidates 4 policy:checkpoint --policy.config pi_modified_bc_rl --policy.dir /root/lehome_winner/checkpoints/lehome_sim` (identical to weekend.ps1:21); ports now: 8000 True, 8767 True, 8766 False.
confirmed.fix: In Ensure-Teacher, when the 8000 branch had to restart the teacher, also kill any process matching '15_winner_relay' and fall through to the relay restart branch (set a flag). Optionally in 22_replay treat `rsp is None` as a retryable relay outage.

(2) 15_winner_relay.py:169-170 wraps the entire TCP accept loop in one `async with websockets.connect(WS_URL, ping_interval=None)`; the per-connection handler at :207 catches only `(ConnectionResetError, ConnectionAbortedError)`. On the relay's actual interpreter (pythoncore-3.14, websockets 17.0.1) `ConnectionClosed.__mro__` is [ConnectionClosed, WebSocketException, Exception, ...] and `issubclass(ConnectionClosed, (ConnectionResetError, ConnectionAbortedError))` is False, so a `ws.send` on the dead socket inside `policy.act` (:115) escapes `main()`, `asyncio.run` re-raises, the process exits (the `finally` at :209-211 closes the Isaac conn first). The `reset` message (:195-198) never touches `ws`, so 22_replay's reset handshake (22_replay_snapshots.py:240-241) succeeds and the failure surfaces on the very first action request, exactly as claimed. (3) 22_replay_snapshots.py:253-254 (claim cited 231-232; minor line offset) does `rsp = recv_msg(conn); act = np.asarray(rsp["action"], ...)` with no None check; `recv_msg` returns None on EOF (:70-71); the TypeError is caught by the single outer `except Exception` at :292 which writes `EXCEPTION:` and falls through to `app.close()`, so the whole garment's recovery run (all snapshots) is lost, not just one attempt. (4) The live relay (PIDs 36832 launcher / 32860 python, created 09-04 10:23:42) is `15_winner_relay.py` with no args, i.e. default WS_URL ws://localhost:8000, so it is the process at risk. (5) Next loop iteration: relay has exited so 8767 is down, Ensure-Teacher's second branch restarts it, so damage is bounded to one garment as claimed. (6) Supporting real-world evidence: sweep.log:12150-12155 shows the identical `rsp["action"]` -> `TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable` traceback from 14_benchmark.py:145 (same client pattern), so the recv-None leg has already occurred in practice. Live process check (Get-CimInstance Win32_Process) shows no process executing weekend.ps1; the only weekend chain running is weekend2.ps1 (PID 33068, started 2026-09-05 16:18:15, file written 16:17:59, marker file weekend2_markers.log = "09-05 16:18  A wait curation"). weekend2.ps1 Stage A (lines 78-85) already implements exactly the proposed fix: inside the poll loop it runs `$alive = Get-CimInstance Win32_Process | Where-Object { $_.CommandLine -match 'curation\.ps1' }` and `if (-not $alive) { Mark "A curation process gone - proceeding"; break }`. So the claimed failure scenario ("curation dies -> weekend chain sleeps until Monday with B-E unexecuted") cannot occur for the running chain; if curation.ps1 (PID 31348, still alive, child lerobot-train PID 4740 running since 12:42) dies for any reason, weekend2.ps1 breaks out within one 300 s cycle. The self-match pitfall does not apply here either: weekend2's own command line contains only 'weekend2.ps1', not 'curation.ps1'. Confirmed for the record: weekend.ps1:63 indeed has no process-alive or deadline check, curation.ps1 emits CURATION-DONE/FAILED only at lines 12, 28, 61, and curation_chain.log is 0 bytes -- but that file is dead code now (superseded at 16:18; weekend_markers.log frozen at its 12:42 entry). Residual, out-of-claim gap: neither script has a hard deadline for a curation process that is alive but hung (e.g. a stuck lerobot-train or benchmark); that is a different scenario from the one claimed and is not evidenced by anything in the current state.

Code-level claim confirmed: weekend.ps1:63 loops on `Select-String ... "CURATION-DONE|FAILED"` with no process-alive check and no deadline, and curation.ps1 emits those sentinels only at lines 12, 28 and 61 (Write-Host on explicit exit/success paths). A silent death of the curation powershell (PID 31348, still alive, training at 36.3k/60k in train_cur.log) would leave curation_chain.log without a sentinel and weekend.ps1 would loop indefinitely. The success path is sound: Write-Host from a Start-Process-redirected powershell.exe does reach the log (weekend.log / weekend2.log contain the Mark text), and curation_chain.log was created at the same second the curation process started (11:13:13), so CURATION-DONE will land there on normal completion. The case-insensitive `FAILED` false-positive angle is also not a practical risk: historical chain logs that carry full Isaac Sim stdout (overnight.log, recover.log, auto_chain2/3.log, 2500+ warning lines each) contain zero case-insensitive 'failed' matches, and 14_benchmark.py / lehome_scene.py / run_full_bench.ps1 never print the word.

However, the finding's `affects_running_chain: true` is stale. No powershell process with `weekend.ps1` in its command line exists anymore (weekend_markers.log stops at `12:42 A wait curation`); the live orchestrator is weekend2.ps1 (PID 33068, launched 16:18:15, marker `16:18 A wait curation`), and its stage-A loop at lines 80-84 already contains exactly the proposed process-alive fallback (`Get-CimInstance Win32_Process | ? CommandLine -match 'curation\.ps1'` -> `Mark "A curation process gone - proceeding"; break`). The regex does not match weekend2's own shell or the bash watchers (their command lines contain `curation_chain.log`, not `curation.ps1`). Residual gap in weekend2: no hard deadline, so a curation process that is alive but hung (e.g. a stuck 14_benchmark.py in the eval loop, which has no timeout) would still block stage A; that is a different, lower-probability scenario than the one claimed.

Impact lens: this cannot change any measured number, cannot burn GPU-hours (the failure mode is an idle GPU until someone notices), and cannot corrupt data; worst case for the superseded weekend.ps1 was lost weekend wall-clock. With weekend2.ps1 running, even that is mitigated. Also noted in passing: the old bash watcher (PIDs 39096/36464) still polls weekend_markers.log for WEEKEND-DONE and will never exit, but that is harmless.

The line-63 observation is literally correct for weekend.ps1 (the poll loop has no process-alive or deadline exit and curation.ps1 only prints CURATION-DONE/FAILED on its three explicit paths), but the finding does not apply to the running chain: no process is executing weekend.ps1 any more. Both halves fail against the current code and the chain that is actually running.

(1) CSV writer: 14_benchmark.py (mtime 2026-09-05 16:15) no longer builds fieldnames from rows[0]. Lines 48-49 define a fixed CSV_FIELDS list (11 keys) and lines 200-204 use `csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=CSV_FIELDS, extrasaction="ignore")` with an explicit comment that this was done so a first-row PLACE_FAIL cannot break the columns; DictWriter's default restval="" fills the 7 missing keys of a 4-key PLACE_FAIL row. No ValueError path remains, so app.close() is not skipped by this route.

(2) Top-up: weekend.ps1 is NOT the running chain. Get-CimInstance shows powershell running weekend2.ps1 (PID 33068, marker log started 16:18) and curation.ps1 (PID 31348); there is no weekend.ps1 process (its marker log stopped at 12:42 "A wait curation"). weekend2.ps1 Full-Eval (lines 52-65) already computes `$need = 10 - [int]$rows[$gd.Name]` and passes `--episodes $need`, with a distinct seed offset (140+$i) and a server-restart check, i.e. exactly the proposed fix. Residual (dormant nit, not the finding as stated): curation.ps1:53-56 still passes `--episodes 10` for any garment with <10 rows. But the trigger is narrower than claimed: reset_episode returns a plain bool (lehome_scene.py:419) and a PLACE_FAIL still appends a row (14_benchmark.py:141-143), so placement failures keep the count at 10; the attachShape flake per HANDOFF.md:131 skips the whole garment (0 rows), for which a 10-episode rerun is exactly right. So affects_running_chain is false for the cited file. Only residual: the already-parsed in-memory curation.ps1 (lines 53-56, --episodes 10, seed 110+$i) retains the over-top-up behavior for its cur_n5 eval (~3.6 h away) and cannot be patched in place. That path has never fired in any 12-garment run (bench_final_n5, big45_n5, all700*, etc. are all exactly 10 rows x 12 garments, 0 PLACE_FAIL; every non-10 CSV is a deliberate 8/5/3-episode sweep). Partially confirmed, partially stale. (1) The CSV-writer half is REFUTED: 14_benchmark.py (mtime 2026-09-05 16:15, after weekend.ps1 started 12:42 and while it is still in stage A) already uses a fixed CSV_FIELDS list (lines 48-49) and `csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=CSV_FIELDS, extrasaction="ignore")` (line 201) with a comment explicitly targeting the first-row-PLACE_FAIL case; missing keys are padded by restval='', so no ValueError, no lost rows, no skipped app.close() from that path. Every driver spawns 14_benchmark.py fresh, so the running chain uses the fixed file. (2) The top-up half is CONFIRMED in code: weekend.ps1:46-48 and curation.ps1:53-56 run `--episodes 10` for any garment with <10 rows and append to the same tag CSV; analyze_bench.py:28 averages over rows, so a partial garment would be over-weighted. But it is a deliberate convention (orchestrator.py:422-432 uses the same full-EVAL_EPISODES rerun), the documented flake mode (AUDIT.md:62, HANDOFF.md:132) is the garment being skipped entirely (0 rows) for which 10 IS the deficit, reruns use distinct seeds so rows are independent draws, and across all 34 bench_*.csv files no garment has ever had a partial count (the one observed mid-run exception, aug_n5_cons3 Seen_2, produced 0 rows). The client (14_benchmark.py:145-146) sends `{"reset": True}` and waits for the ack before the first observation of every episode, so stale actions from a prior episode cannot be executed; the same reset also covers the new-connection path (accept at line 137) since no action is served before the first reset. proposals.title: Two-seed action-averaging ensemble at inference (champion + seed2), evaluated on the 120-episode protocol -- no training, ~25-line server patch
proposals.rationale: Stage B delivers a second champion-recipe model (seed 2000) by ~Sun 04:45. Averaging the per-step actions of two independently trained BC policies is the cheapest known variance reducer for ACT-class students and is exactly the 'avoid the very bad chunk' effect the paper attributes to best-of-N (§7.4) -- without the value head we lack. The champion's biggest losses vs the teacher are on garments with plenty of data (Seen_6: teacher 7-10/10, student 4/10; Unseen_0: 7-9 vs 5), i.e. student execution variance, not data starvation. The existing --consensus (medoid over input-noise) is a different, untested mechanism; --ensemble (temporal) was measured ineffective (37.5%). Both models share dataset stats (r3plus) so averaging after post-processing is stat-safe, and averaging after post() also stays correct if a cur-trained model is added later.
proposals.expected_gain: +1 to +4pp on the 120-ep protocol is the typical range for a 2-model BC ensemble; 0 is possible. Roughly one Seen_6/Unseen_0 episode each. Also yields, for free, a smoothing effect on the n_action_steps=5 replanning jitter. Not a headline-changing lever alone, but it stacks on top of proposal 1 (ensemble the 120k models next week).
proposals.how: Patch C:\Users\H\Desktop\lehome-win\12_policy_server.py (Python re-reads the file on each Start-Process; no chain relaunch needed): accept `sys.argv[1]` as a comma-separated list; build `policies = [ACTPolicy.from_pretrained(c).to('cuda').eval() for c in ckpts]` and per-policy `(pre_i, post_i) = make_pre_post_processors(p.config, pretrained_path=c, ...)`; set `p.config.n_action_steps = N` on every policy; on `{reset}` call `p.reset()` for all; on each observation compute `acts = [post_i(p.select_action(pre_i(obs_copy))) for ...]` (each policy keeps its own 5-step queue; they stay in lockstep because reset and every step hit all of them) and reply with `np.mean(acts, axis=0)`. Refuse `--consensus > 1` when len(policies) > 1. Serve: `12_policy_server.py outputs\act_student_r3plus_aug\checkpoints\060000\pretrained_model,outputs\act_student_seed2\checkpoints\060000\pretrained_model --n-action-steps 5`; then `run_full_bench.ps1 -Episodes 10 -Tag ens2_n5 -Port 8766 -PhysPerAction 2` plus the per-garment top-up loop. Compare against bench_final_n5.csv (47.5%) and bench_seed2_n5.csv; if chunk30 (stage H) is >= champion, also run a 3-model average (per-step outputs, so mixed chunk sizes are fine). Smoke-test first with `--check` and one Seen_2 episode (`14_benchmark.py --garment-dir Top_Long_Seen_2 --episodes 1 --port 8766 --phys-per-action 2`).
proposals.risk: Averaging two policies can produce mean-of-modes actions at genuinely bimodal decision points (which arm reaches first); folding here is a fairly fixed sequence, so the risk is modest but non-zero. Two forward passes per step: ACT 51.7M is a few ms, well inside the 33 ms budget. Requires B to finish; if seed2 scores far below the champion (>10pp), the average may drag down rather than lift -- check bench_seed2_n5 before spending the 2h. Patch is untested code in the serving path; keep the single-checkpoint code path unchanged for all other evals.

proposals.title: Audit the Seen_8 success judge (CPU-only): condition d3 = d(0,1) >= thr is unsatisfiable by construction in every recorded episode
proposals.rationale: Seen_8 is 0/10 for every student and 0-2/10 for the teacher (whose authors report 80%+ across garments), costing 8.3pp of the headline ceiling (champion is 51.8% on the other 110 episodes). The CSVs show why: in all 30 Seen_8 rows across bench_final_n5 / bench_full3 / bench_big45_n5, d3 sits at 3.66-4.36 against thr[3] = 10.8, with near-zero variance -- i.e. keypoints 0 and 1 are ~4 cm apart on this shirt regardless of what the policy does, whereas the same metric is 15-16 for Seen_3 (thr 9.6) and passes routinely. d3 is a 'spread' condition (d(0,1) >= thr, lehome_scene.py:500-501), so points 0 and 1 are meant to be far apart (shoulder/collar ends). A constant ~4 cm strongly suggests map_check_points (lehome_scene.py:238) mapped index 0 or 1 to a wrong vertex for Seen_8, making the garment un-passable by construction -- HANDOFF §5-4 already suspected a 'success-condition conflict'. Several teacher episodes in bench_full3 reach n_pass=3 with d0/d1/d2 within a few cm of threshold, so real folds are happening and being scored 0.
proposals.expected_gain: Two outcomes, both worth having: (a) mapping bug confirmed and fixed -> re-scored Seen_8 could add +3 to +8pp to the headline (each Seen_8 success is +0.83pp) and Seen_8 becomes collectable, unlocking teacher data for it (today: zero Seen_8 training episodes anywhere); (b) mapping matches the official garment_config -> Seen_8 is provably unpassable in this replica and the paper can legitimately report 110-episode numbers (51.8%) with a footnote, instead of carrying an 8.3pp handicap. Either way the reported number improves or becomes defensible.
proposals.how: CPU-only, can run right now in parallel with the training chain (no GPU, no process interaction). (1) With the existing diagnostics (recon_01_garment.py / recon_03_baked_points.py, or a 30-line script importing lehome_scene.map_check_points) print, for Seen_8 and a passing garment such as Seen_3: gcfg['success_distance'], scale, the raw check-point coordinates in the official config, the mapped vertex indices, and the rest-pose pairwise distances d(0,4), d(2,3), d(1,5), d(0,1), d(4,5). Expect d(0,1) at rest to be ~shoulder width (well above 10.8) for a correct mapping; if it is ~4, find the nearest-vertex tie or index-order assumption that broke for Seen_8's mesh ordering. Cross-check against the official LeHome checker in the lehome_solution/WSL copy for the same garment. (2) Only if a mapping bug is confirmed: fix map_check_points for that case, then a 15-minute GPU confirmation -- `14_benchmark.py --garment-dir Top_Long_Seen_8 --garment-type Top_Long --episodes 10 --steps 600 --port 8766 --tag seen8fix_n5 --seed 8 --reset-mode initial --phys-per-action 2` against the champion server -- and re-score the existing bench CSVs' d-values offline where possible. (3) Write the finding into HANDOFF §5-4 and PROJECT_REPORT either way; if unpassable, adopt 'all 120 / Seen_8 excluded 110' dual reporting as AUDIT §C already recommends.
proposals.risk: It may be the official judge's own quirk (the winning team also reports lower rates on some garments), in which case changing the checker would break comparability with the official benchmark -- fix only if our mapping demonstrably differs from the official one. Re-running the judge changes scores of past CSVs only for Seen_8, so document the re-scoring explicitly. Requires ~1-2h of a person's or an agent's attention, not GPU time.

proposals.title: Quantify evaluation noise: replicate the champion's 120-episode benchmark with a disjoint seed set
proposals.rationale: Every headline number (student 47.5, big45 44.2, teacher 45.8/45.8, cur/seed2/cur2 to come) is a single 120-episode run with the SAME drop seeds 1-12 (run_full_bench.ps1 line 27: --seed $i). A binomial 95% interval at p=0.475, n=120 is roughly 38.7-56.4%, i.e. +-9 %p, so none of the top-3 results are currently distinguishable, and the teacher's own two runs (bench_full2 vs bench_full3, both 45.8%) disagree by up to 6/10 on single garments (Seen_4: 0/10 vs 6/10). The Monday report cannot claim 'student = teacher' or 'big45 < champion' without a measured replicate. Stage B measures TRAINING-seed variance only; nothing in the chain measures EVAL-seed variance, which is the cheaper and more fundamental term.
proposals.expected_gain: No performance gain. Produces (a) a second 120-ep estimate of the champion, (b) a pooled 240-ep estimate with CI ~ +-6.3 %p, (c) a per-garment seed-sensitivity table showing which garments (Seen_0/3/7/8, Unseen_1) are truly weak vs. noisy. Most likely outcome: champion, big45 and teacher fall inside one interval and the report says 'parity within noise' honestly; if the replicate lands below ~40% the 47.5 headline is a lucky draw and must be rewritten.
proposals.how:
Run in a window where the chain is training and NOT in Full-Eval (Full-Eval's Stop-Student kills every 12_policy_server and 12_policy_server has no --port flag, so overlap is fatal). Safe windows: Sat 16:40-18:40 (A train, cur reaches 60k ~18:40), Sat ~20:40-Sun ~02:40 (B train), Sun ~04:40-11:00 (stage C, no training, GPU freest). Commands (PowerShell, from C:\Users\H\Desktop\lehome-win):
  Start-Process C:\Users\H\Desktop\lerobot\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -ArgumentList '12_policy_server.py','outputs\act_student_r3plus_aug\checkpoints\060000\pretrained_model','--n-action-steps','5' -RedirectStandardOutput server_final_rep.log
  then for i=1..12 over the sorted Top_Long garment dirs:
  C:\isaacsim\python.bat 14_benchmark.py --garment-dir <g> --garment-type Top_Long --episodes 10 --steps 600 --port 8766 --tag final_n5_rep --seed (200+i) --reset-mode initial --phys-per-action 2
  Analysis: per-garment k/10 for bench_final_n5.csv vs bench_final_n5_rep.csv, pooled rate with Wilson CI, and paired (same-seed) comparisons only for configs that used seeds 1-12. Verify Group-Object garment counts == 10 before quoting.
proposals.risk: Concurrent Isaac Sim + student server next to lerobot-train: GPU is 21.5/32.6 GB used with util ~0% (dataloader-bound) and 91 GB RAM free, so memory is fine, but CPU contention may slow the running training by 10-20% and shift the chain later; PhysX attachShape flake can drop a garment (re-run that garment with the same seed). If a chain Full-Eval starts mid-run the server is killed and the benchmark silently talks to the chain's server -> discard any rows written after the chain's marker time.

proposals.title: Checkpoint-selection ablation: evaluate the champion's 020000 and 040000 checkpoints under the identical n5 protocol
proposals.rationale: The chain (weekend.ps1 lines 69/101/109), curation.ps1 and orchestrator all hard-code checkpoints\060000 as the thing to evaluate; nothing has ever shown that 60k is on a plateau rather than past or before the optimum. This also directly bears on the epoch-confound finding (700-ep models get 8 epochs, 267-ep champion 21.5): a 3-point learning curve for the champion (20k/40k/60k = 7/14/21.5 epochs) is the minimum evidence for saying whether the data-scaling runs were undertrained. outputs\act_student_r3plus_aug\checkpoints\{020000,040000} already exist (saved 08-26 19:38 and 22:40), so this is eval-only.
proposals.expected_gain: Two more 120-ep points paired (seeds 1-12) with bench_final_n5.csv. Likely result: 20k well below 47.5 (undertrained), 40k within +-5 %p of 60k. If 40k >= 60k, the '60k budget' recipe and the choice of checkpoint for seed2/cur2 evaluations become selection questions and the report must present 'best of 3 checkpoints' with the noise caveat from proposal 1. Optional extension (+4 h, only if stage C runs long): all700b 040000/060000 comparison already exists at 060000 (30.8%); adding its 040000 gives a second curve at matched STEPS so the epoch-vs-capacity attribution is at least two-sided.
proposals.how:
Same window rules as proposal 1. Two passes, each: start 12_policy_server.py on outputs\act_student_r3plus_aug\checkpoints\020000\pretrained_model (then 040000) with --n-action-steps 5; run
  powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File run_full_bench.ps1 -Episodes 10 -Tag aug20k_n5 -Port 8766 -PhysPerAction 2   (second pass -Tag aug40k_n5)
  which reproduces seeds 1-12 so every episode is paired with bench_final_n5.csv; back-fill any garment with <10 rows using 14_benchmark.py --seed (130+i) exactly as Full-Eval does; kill the server (Get-CimInstance Win32_Process | ? CommandLine -match '12_policy_server' | % { Stop-Process -Id $_.ProcessId }). Report the curve as epochs (7.2 / 14.3 / 21.5) next to steps.
proposals.risk: Same concurrency/overlap risks as proposal 1. Interpretation risk: with +-9 %p per point a monotone-looking curve can still be noise; state it as such and do not pick the best checkpoint post hoc for the headline unless proposal 1's replicate is also run on it.

proposals.title: Augmentation ablation on the full protocol: act_student_r3plus (aug OFF, same 267 episodes, 60k) with --n-action-steps 5
proposals.rationale: 'Augmentation ON' is presented as an ingredient of the champion recipe (HANDOFF 0, weekend.ps1 Train-Std forces image_transforms), but the evidence is contradictory and tiny: 4-garment x 8 sweep gives noaug_n5 59.4 vs aug_n5 65.6 (a 2-episode difference), while at n100 the same sweep gives noaug 40.6 > aug 31.2 and the 120-ep runs give noaug 28.3 (bench_r3plus60k) < aug 31. The aug-OFF twin checkpoint outputs\act_student_r3plus\checkpoints\060000 already exists, so the full 120-episode, seed-paired ablation costs one eval and closes the only recipe-level ablation that is still open. Stage B (seed2) does not address this.
proposals.expected_gain: One paired 120-ep number for aug OFF at n5. Expected: within +-9 %p of 47.5, i.e. 'augmentation not shown to matter at 267 episodes / 21 epochs' -- which is what the report should then say instead of listing aug as a proven ingredient. If noaug_n5 >= aug_n5 the recipe used by stages B/D/E is not the demonstrated best and this must be flagged before those numbers are interpreted. Unseen_0/1 rows are the ones to watch, since the aug claim was motivated by Unseen collapse.
proposals.how:
Same window rules. Start 12_policy_server.py outputs\act_student_r3plus\checkpoints\060000\pretrained_model --n-action-steps 5; run
  powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File run_full_bench.ps1 -Episodes 10 -Tag noaug_n5_full -Port 8766 -PhysPerAction 2
(seeds 1-12, paired with bench_final_n5.csv and bench_r3plus60k.csv); back-fill <10-row garments with 14_benchmark.py --seed (130+i); stop the server. Present as a 2x2 table (aug x n_action_steps {100,5}) on 120 episodes: noaug/n100 28.3 (bench_r3plus60k), aug/n100 31 (existing), aug/n5 47.5 (bench_final_n5), noaug/n5 = this run; note the 32-episode sweep as supporting data only.
proposals.risk: Low. Same concurrency caveats. If the r3plus 060000 checkpoint was trained with a different chunk/dim (verify its train_config.json shows chunk_size 100, dim 512, lr 1e-5 like the aug twin) the comparison is confounded; check before running.

proposals.title: Replace stage E (cur240 low-res) with an epoch-matched continuation of act_student_cur to 113k steps
proposals.rationale: The report's data-scaling conclusion ('700 episodes did not help: 3.3 / 30.8 / 44.2 vs 47.5') compares models at equal STEPS, not equal EPOCHS: r3plus is 44,700 frames (60k x 16 = 21.5 epochs), cur is 84,405 frames (11.4 epochs at 60k), all700 is 116,010 (8.3 epochs). No queued stage fixes this. ACT has no LR scheduler (configuration_act.py get_scheduler_preset returns None, lr constant 1e-5), so resuming cur's 060000 checkpoint to 113k steps is a genuine longer run, not a warm-restart artifact; lerobot applies CLI overrides on top of the checkpoint config on resume (parser.py:311 from_pretrained(cli_args=...)) and recover700b.ps1 already exercised the resume path cleanly (finding: all700b->c resume verified clean). Stage E, by contrast, answers a speed question (AUDIT D row 2), evaluates a 240x320 model that the server now resizes for anyway (12_policy_server.py lines 111-163), inherits the stage-C LEHOME_RAND_LIGHT/TABLE_TEX leak into its eval, and costs ~9.5 h (1.5 h convert + 6 h train + 2 h eval) vs ~7.3 h here.
proposals.expected_gain: The single experiment that can separate 'more data does not help this student' from 'more data was not trained long enough'. If cur@113k (21.5 epochs, 505 episodes) lands >= ~55% it beats the champion beyond the +-9 %p noise and the report's scaling story flips; if it stays ~45-50% the null data-scaling result becomes defensible at matched epochs (at least for 505 eps). Either outcome is reportable; the current step-matched comparison is not. Side benefit: a 060000 -> 080000 -> 100000 -> 113000 curve for cur, complementing proposal 2.
proposals.how:
Requires relaunching weekend.ps1, which is still in the stage-A polling loop (weekend_markers.log has only '09-05 12:42 A wait curation'; PowerShell parsed the file at launch so on-disk edits do nothing). Relaunch cost is zero work lost; do it while curation's eval is running (~18:40-20:40 Sat) so B still starts on time. In the relaunched copy, replace lines 104-110 with:
  Mark "E resume cur to 113k"
  & $train "--config_path=$base\outputs\act_student_cur\checkpoints\060000\pretrained_model\train_config.json" "--resume=true" "--steps=113000" "--save_freq=20000" *>> "$base\train_cur113k.log"
  $ck = "$base\outputs\act_student_cur\checkpoints\113000\pretrained_model"
  if (Test-Path $ck) { Mark "E eval cur113k"; Full-Eval $ck "cur113k_n5"; Mark "E done" } else { Mark "E TRAIN FAILED" }
(checkpoint dir name follows lerobot's zero-padded step; confirm with Get-ChildItem outputs\act_student_cur\checkpoints after the run). While relaunching, also add `Remove-Item Env:LEHOME_RAND_LIGHT, Env:LEHOME_RAND_TABLE_TEX -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` after line 83 so D and E evaluate under the same conditions as seed2/cur/final. Timeline at 2.5-3 step/s: +53k steps ~5.3 h, eval ~2 h; with D ending ~20:00 Sun this finishes ~03:30 Mon, inside the 10:00 window with ~2 h more slack than stage E had.
proposals.risk: Requires killing and relaunching weekend.ps1 (user decision; do not kill it from the audit). If lerobot 0.6.1 refuses the --steps override on resume, fall back to editing steps in the checkpoint's train_config.json copy (config_path can point at a copied directory) -- test with --check-style dry run is not available, so run it first for 100 steps into a scratch --output_dir to confirm the override takes. Continuation only tests 505 eps; the 700-ep matched run (156k steps, ~9 h from all700b's 060000) does not fit before Monday and should be stated as future work. Loses the low-res result, which AUDIT D row 2 wanted; it can run Monday after the report since the server-side resize is already in place.

proposals.title: Turn every Full-Eval into a hard-mining source: snapshot student failures in 14_benchmark, then let the teacher recover from them (automatic DAgger) into distill_data_recov so stage D ingests it with no weekend.ps1 edit
proposals.rationale: The student (47.5%) already equals the teacher (45.8%) because filtered BC discards teacher failures. The only mechanism in the paper notes that can push a student past its teacher is the one the author could not use: an automatic expert correcting the STUDENT's own failure states (LEHOME_paper_notes.md §E). Stage C as queued replays TEACHER failure states (distill_data_r4_fail), which corrects the teacher's distribution, not the student's. Meanwhile the chain will run three 120-episode student evals this weekend (cur_n5 tonight ~18:30, seed2_n5 Sun ~02:30, cur2_n5 Sun ~17:30), each producing ~60-70 failed episodes that are currently thrown away. 14_benchmark.py is re-read by Python at every per-garment launch, so an additive edit landing before ~18:30 Sat needs no relaunch of the running chain. 22_replay_snapshots.py globs `{GARMENT_DIR}_*` under --src and already groups by robot_z (student eval is always z=0.5, so all snapshots agree), and weekend.ps1 stage D builds cur2 from 'distill_data_recov' by directory scan, so writing the student-recovery episodes to --out distill_data_recov makes them flow into cur2 automatically; junction names keep the source tag (…recov__Top_Long_Seen_3_cur_n5_e004_snap_0299_s5001_r0) so teacher-recovery and student-recovery can be separated later.
proposals.expected_gain: Data: ~15-25 student-recovery episodes per eval pass (65 fails x 2 tries x assumed 15-25% teacher recovery yield; yield is unmeasured — the only replay smoke so far was 0/2 on Seen_3 success mode). Effect on the 120-episode score this weekend: not detectable (95% CI is about +/-9pp at n=120); the honest readout is per-garment 20-30 episodes on Seen_3/Seen_0/Seen_7 next week. Strategic value is high: it is the first data whose states come from the student's own distribution, i.e. the only lever that addresses compounding error rather than teacher coverage.
proposals.how: 1) Edit C:\Users\H\Desktop\lehome-win\14_benchmark.py (additive only, before the cur_n5 eval starts): inside the step loop add `if i % 100 == 99 and i < N_STEPS - 1: snaps.append((i, view.get_world_positions().cpu().numpy(), view.get_velocities().cpu().numpy(), left/right joint positions))` (same keys as 16_collect_distill.save_snap: step, cloth_pos, cloth_vel, qL, qR, robot_z=LS.ROBOT_Z); after the episode, `if not success:` write them with np.savez_compressed to `distill_data_stud_fail/{GARMENT_DIR}_{TAG}_e{ep:03d}/snap_{i:04d}.npz` plus meta.json {garment, tag, ep, success: false, n_pass}. Wrap the whole thing in try/except so it can never alter CSV rows or the app.close() path. Cost per failed episode ~1 MB, ~5 ms. 2) After each eval finishes (watch weekend_markers.log for 'B eval seed2' -> 'B done'), run per weak garment on the second relay from proposal 3: `C:\isaacsim\python.bat 22_replay_snapshots.py --src distill_data_stud_fail --out distill_data_recov --mode recover --garment-dir Top_Long_Seen_3 --per-snap 2 --max-snaps 15 --port 8768 --seed 5001` (then Seen_0 seed 5002, Seen_7 5003, Seen_6 5004, Seen_5 5005, Seen_1 5006; never Unseen_0/1 — they must stay unseen). Set `$env:LEHOME_RAND_LIGHT=1; $env:LEHOME_RAND_TABLE_TEX=1` in that shell only. ~15 snaps x 2 x ~90 s + 3 min Isaac boot = ~50 min per garment. 3) Record in HANDOFF that cur2 (stage D) contains teacher-recovery AND student-recovery episodes if the Sun ~10:00 'D build cur2' marker comes after your replays finish; otherwise the data is used in the first post-weekend training.
proposals.risk: Editing 14_benchmark.py while the chain is polling: a bug in the snapshot path could abort a garment's episodes -> mitigated by try/except and by testing once with `--episodes 1 --steps 100 --tag snaptest` against the student server BEFORE 18:30 (uses the GPU for ~2 min; the training slows briefly). Restoring states produced under --phys-per-action 2 into a teacher rollout at 1 physics step per action is fine (states are valid physics states), but PhysX may occasionally explode on set_velocities of a grasped cloth — 22_replay already discards non-successes. If the 8000 teacher dies during stage C, Ensure-Teacher restarts it and kills your relay's WebSocket; the replay process then raises and must be restarted by hand. Mixing student-recovery into cur2 confounds stage D's 'curated + teacher recovery' comparison — acceptable only if logged.

proposals.title: Replace stage C's snapshot pick (snap_0499 of whatever fails) with semi-success-first selection scored offline from cloth_pos, and add a replay-yield ledger
proposals.rationale: 22_replay_snapshots.py recover mode currently takes `mid[-2]` = snap_0499 of each failed episode: a state 100 steps before timeout, chosen without looking at how close to success it was. The collection logs show the pool is rich in near-successes that this ignores: episodes ending with n_pass>=3 are 115/165 for Seen_0, 50/108 Seen_3, 51/72 Seen_1, 23/27 Seen_6, 23/93 Seen_7. The paper's semi-success replay (§3.2, AUDIT B3) is exactly 'retry from the state that already reached the first checkpoint'. The check_idx and thresholds are in scene['check_idx'] / scene['gcfg'] after build_scene, and every snapshot already stores cloth_pos, so n_pass at every saved step can be computed in-process with the same 5-line formula 14_benchmark.py uses (lines 170-177) — zero extra simulation. 22_replay is re-read at each Start-Process, so the edit takes effect for stage C (starts after 'B eval seed2', ~Sun 04:30 at the current pace) without touching weekend.ps1. Yield is the KPI a data engine optimizes and it has never been measured (one smoke run, 0/2).
proposals.expected_gain: Same 24 attempts per garment, so no extra GPU time. Yield multiplier vs the blind snap_0499 pick is unmeasured; a plausible range is 1.5-3x because a 4/5 state is one fold away while a random step-499 state may be a tangled cloth. Even if the multiplier is small, the ledger converts stage C from 'some recovery episodes appeared' into 'yield per (garment, n_pass, step) bucket', which is what Monday's decision about scaling recovery collection needs.
proposals.how: In C:\Users\H\Desktop\lehome-win\22_replay_snapshots.py: (a) move candidate scoring after `scene = build_scene(...)`: for each episode dir, for each snap with 99 <= step <= 499 (skip snap_0005 and the terminal snap_0599), compute `p = d['cloth_pos'].reshape(-1,3)[list(scene['check_idx'])]*100`, `n_pass = sum([d(0,4)<=thr[0], d(2,3)<=thr[1], d(1,5)<=thr[2], d(0,1)>=thr[3], d(4,5)>=thr[4]])` with thr = success_distance*scale as in 14_benchmark; per episode pick the EARLIEST snapshot achieving that episode's max n_pass (the moment it became almost-done, most recoverable); rank episodes by (n_pass desc, step asc), keep the robot_z-major group as now, then `[:MAX_SNAPS]`. Keep --max-snaps 12 --per-snap 2 so stage C's 50-minute WaitForExit still holds. (b) After each attempt append a row to `replay_yield.csv`: mode, garment, src_episode, snap_step, n_pass_at_snap, robot_z, seed, rep, success, succ_step, sec. (c) Log the selection table at start ('Seen_3: 12 snaps, n_pass histogram {4: 7, 3: 5}, steps 199-399'). Test once headless with `--max-snaps 1 --per-snap 1 --out distill_data_r4_replay_smoke --garment-dir Top_Long_Seen_6` (Seen_6 has the highest semi ratio) — ~5 min, needs port 8767 free, so do it only before stage C starts and while no collector is connected, or on the 8768 relay from proposal 3. Update the recover-mode docstring: r4_fail snapshots are 100-step-interval states, not ruin moments.
proposals.risk: check_idx is a per-build vertex mapping; it matches the snapshots only because they were recorded from the same garment USD and build path (16_collect used scene['check_idx'] too) — assert the cloth_pos vertex count equals view.count before scoring and fall back to the old pick if not. Restoring a 4/5 state may hand the teacher a cloth that is geometrically 'almost folded' but physically unstable (velocities); fails are discarded, but yield could still disappoint — that is exactly what the ledger is for. Editing 22_replay after stage C has launched a garment affects only subsequent garments (each is a fresh process), so an inconsistent selection across garments is possible; make the edit before the 'B eval seed2' marker appears.

proposals.title: Make the relay multi-client (--port / --session-id) and run a second Isaac sim during the stage-C window — the WSL server already batches concurrent sessions, only 15_winner_relay.py serializes us
proposals.rationale: The paper's collection engine runs 3-5 sims against one stateless policy server (§3.1). Reading /root/lehome_winner/lehome_solution/scripts/serve.py in WSL: it is explicitly designed to serve 'multiple concurrent workers, each with its own session', with an InferenceBatcher that drains concurrent requests into one forward pass ('~Nx throughput with N concurrent workers'). Our bottleneck is entirely 15_winner_relay.py: TCP_PORT is hardcoded 8767, session_id is hardcoded 'isaac', it listen(1)s and handles one connection at a time — which is why PARALLEL_SIMS=2 killed the orchestrator's second collector. A second relay process on 8768 with a distinct session_id is a 6-line patch and does not touch the running 8767 relay (keep the defaults so weekend.ps1's Ensure-Teacher restart still works). During stage C (~Sun 04:30-10:00) the GPU carries only teacher + one Isaac sim; that window and the ~6 h slack after WEEKEND-DONE (~Mon 02:30-04:00 by measured rates: 60k steps ~6 h, 120-ep eval 1 h 50 m, stage C ~5.5 h, converts ~1.5 h each) are where proposals 1 and 4 run without touching the chain.
proposals.expected_gain: Roughly 1.8x teacher-side collection throughput whenever two sims run (relay side is per-connection; server side batches; sim step time dominates). Concretely ~200 extra teacher attempts in the 5.5 h stage-C window and ~250 more in the Monday slack, i.e. the sim time that proposals 1 and 4 need. No direct effect on success rate; it is the enabler. The 0.5 h is a smoke test of two simultaneous clients.
proposals.how: Patch C:\Users\H\Desktop\lehome-win\15_winner_relay.py: `TCP_PORT = int(sys.argv[sys.argv.index('--port')+1]) if '--port' in sys.argv else 8767`; `SESSION_ID = sys.argv[sys.argv.index('--session-id')+1] if '--session-id' in sys.argv else 'isaac'` and use it in `req['session_id']`. Launch: `Start-Process C:\Users\H\AppData\Local\Microsoft\WindowsApps\python.exe -ArgumentList '15_winner_relay.py','--port','8768','--session-id','isaac2' -RedirectStandardOutput relay2.log -RedirectStandardError relay2.err.log -WorkingDirectory C:\Users\H\Desktop\lehome-win`. Smoke test (before stage C, i.e. while 8767 is idle): two concurrent `14_benchmark.py --garment-dir Top_Long_Seen_6 --episodes 2 --steps 200 --port 8767|8768 --tag relay2test` and confirm both CSVs get rows and relay2.log shows 'Isaac 연결' plus per-50-step preds. Check `nvidia-smi` before adding a sim while training runs: now 21.5 GB used with training + teacher; a second Isaac process needs ~4-5 GB, so it fits but expect 10-20% training slowdown — restrict the second sim to the stage-C window and post-WEEKEND-DONE unless stage E's finish time has slack. Later (not this weekend) the same patch unblocks orchestrator PARALLEL_SIMS=2 by passing --port per job.
proposals.risk: If serve.py keys per-session state on session_id only, two relays with distinct ids are safe; if any state is global (e.g. the inpainting anchor), the second worker corrupts the first — the smoke test above detects this (teacher success on Seen_6 should stay ~7-10/10 across both ports). Ensure-Teacher in weekend.ps1 restarts the WSL server if port 8000 drops; that closes relay2's WebSocket, and relay2 does not reconnect — you must restart it by hand (a 3-line reconnect loop in main() would fix it but touch the 8767 code path too; leave the running relay alone). JAX VRAM growth with batched requests is bounded by the batcher's drain window; watch /tmp/wsrv.log for OOM.

proposals.title: Curriculum-weighted fresh teacher collection on the three weakest Seen garments with the ruin-rule snapshotter, camera jitter and per-step light actually ON — the first data ever produced by AUDIT items A1-A4
proposals.rationale: Every claim in AUDIT.md §A ('ruin-moment snapshots', 'camera jitter', 'per-step light') is code that has produced zero episodes: distill_data_r4/r4_fail were collected before those features existed (r4_fail has only 100-step snapshots and no preds.npy), and the curated 505-episode set therefore has none of the augmentations the paper credits for Unseen robustness. Independently, the student's weak garments are also the teacher's data-poorest: r4 has 12 successes for Seen_3 (student 1/10, teacher ~10% yield), 21 for Seen_0 (3/10), 22 for Seen_7 (4/10) versus 37-40 for the strong ones. The paper's curriculum P ∝ e^{3(1-SR)} gives Seen_3 weight 14.9, Seen_0 13.6, Seen_7 11.4 versus ~3-5 for the strong garments, i.e. it would spend ~75% of a collection block on exactly these three. Running this on the second relay (proposal 3) during the stage-C window and the Monday slack costs the chain nothing, and the failures it keeps come with preds.npy + ruin snapshots, which is what makes 22_replay --mode semi and the paper's ruin-moment recovery usable in the next cycle (proposals 1-2 currently have to work with mechanical 100-step states).
proposals.expected_gain: At measured teacher yields (Seen_3 ~10%, Seen_0 ~13%, Seen_7 ~19%) and ~70 s per attempt with --early-kill, a 6 h block split 2.3/2.1/1.7 h yields roughly +12 Seen_3, +14 Seen_0, +17 Seen_7 successes — doubling Seen_3's corpus. Direct student effect if trained next week: perhaps +1-2 successes per 10 on each of those garments, i.e. +2-4pp overall, inside the 120-episode noise but visible in a 30-episode per-garment eval. Secondary, more certain value: ~250 failure episodes with real ruin-moment snapshots and preds.npy (fuel for semi/ruin recovery), and the first episodes carrying cam-jitter/per-step-light so the augmentation claims in AUDIT/PROJECT_REPORT stop being vacuous.
proposals.how: In a fresh PowerShell (never the chain's shell): `$env:LEHOME_RAND_LIGHT='1'; $env:LEHOME_RAND_TABLE_TEX='1'; $env:LEHOME_RAND_CAM='1'; $env:LEHOME_RAND_PERSTEP='1'; $env:LEHOME_DROP_Z_RANGE='0.545,0.63'` then, sequentially: `C:\isaacsim\python.bat 16_collect_distill.py --garment-dir Top_Long_Seen_3 --target-keeps 12 --episodes 120 --steps 600 --port 8768 --out distill_data_r5 --seed 5100 --keep-fail --snapshot --early-kill` (note --target-keeps caps attempts at 3N=36, too few at 10% yield, so either run it 3 times with seeds 5100/5101/5102 or drop --target-keeps and use --episodes 110), then Seen_0 (`--seed 5200`, ~100 attempts), then Seen_7 (`--seed 5300`, ~85 attempts). Keep garment texture swap OFF (LEHOME_RAND_GARMENT_TEX unset) to protect teacher yield, matching the r3 'half' finding. Verify in 16_result_Top_Long_Seen_3_s5100.txt that '[aug] 카메라 지터' and '[망친순간]' lines appear within the first 3 episodes; if '[망친순간]' never fires, the relay is not forwarding success_pred (check relay2.log 'step 50: success=...') — stop and fix before burning hours. Afterwards `17_convert_distill.py --src distill_data_r5 ...` is NOT needed this weekend; add 'distill_data_r5' to the stage-D-style junction list for the first post-weekend training and to orchestrator SOURCE_SHARE.
proposals.risk: Runs against the shared WSL teacher while stage C uses it: server-side batching should absorb two sessions, but if teacher latency doubles, stage C's 50-minute per-garment timeout gets tighter (measured ~39 min today) — watch recov_*.log for 'C timeout' markers and pause this collection if one appears. LEHOME_RAND_CAM perturbs the camera pose the teacher was trained on; the jitter is small (±5 mm/±1°/±3% focal) but if Seen_3 yield drops well below its ~10% baseline in the first 40 attempts, disable it for that garment. Collecting only on weak garments skews cur-style merges toward them; the paper accepts this deliberately (curriculum), but log the per-garment counts in HANDOFF so a later 'Seen_2 regressed' is not misread. Do not collect on Unseen_0/1.

ranked.title: Audit the Seen_8 success judge (CPU-only): condition d3 = d(0,1) >= thr is unsatisfiable by construction in every recorded episode
ranked.why: Verified in bench_final_n5.csv: Seen_8 d3 = 3.74-4.36 vs thr 10.8 on every row while Seen_3 d3 = 15-18; near-zero variance means the metric is policy-independent, i.e. a mapping or spec bug. 0.5 GPU-h, CPU-only, zero interaction with the chain, and both outcomes (fix -> up to +8pp; confirmed unpassable -> defensible 110-ep reporting) improve the report. Best gain/probability/cost ratio by far.
